I found a TV remote in the park and pressed pause.
The pigeon looked at me like I owed it money.
I put a tissue in front of him. Just in case.
A kid's ice cream was frozen halfway to the ground.
I caught it. I ate it.
I pressed play. Nothing. The batteries were dead.
The pigeon sighed. I didn't know pigeons could sigh.
The store was out of double A batteries.
Every store was out of double A batteries.
Of course they were. Everybody who ever found this remote had already looked.
I crossed the ocean on frozen waves. Like stepping stones.
In Paris, I fixed the Mona Lisa's smile.
Then I put it back. She looked wrong happy.
In Japan, a bullet train was stopped at full speed.
I sat in first class. It didn't go anywhere, but the seats were nice.
The pigeon followed me the whole way. Walking.
It refused to fly in a paused world. It was the principle.
A year passed. Probably. The clocks didn't agree.
I grew a beard. The pigeon grew a beard.
In a tiny shop in Iceland, I found one battery. Just one.
I sat down in the snow.
The pigeon walked over, and lifted its wing.
Under it was the other battery. It had been carrying it the whole time.
It looked at the beard. It looked at the frozen ocean.
It had wanted to see the world.
The man sneezed into his tissue.
The kid looked at his empty hand.
I put the remote back on the bench. Exactly where I found it.
A guy sat down and picked it up. Is this yours?
The pigeon landed next to him. It winked at me.
